_note: Registry intent for file associations, applied by tweaks.ps1. Data only - the script holds the algorithm.
_scope: What CAN be scripted. Default-app choices (UserChoice) are hash-protected by Windows and must be set through Settings > Default apps.

markdown._why: GenOffice's handler never launched from a double-click even with a correct ProgId, a quoted command and an Applications registration - while 'Open with > GenOffice' worked. A plain notepad.exe handler copies the pattern that demonstrably works for PotPlayer: ordinary exe, quoted path, existing Applications entry. Notepad++ was removed on 16 Nov; this is the inbox notepad.exe that still exists in System32.
markdown._removeWhen: Double-click on .md launches again and the app picker works, i.e. notes/windows-shell-repair.md 'Repair path' steps 2-3 have been taken. Then point .md back at GenOffice and delete MarkdownText, this block's _why, and the notepad.exe OpenWithList entry. Until that day this is a stopgap, not the intended design - do not copy it to another machine as if it were.

_appRegistrationWhy: Windows resolves an OpenWithList entry by executable name, which only works for applications registered under HKCR\Applications\<exe>. PotPlayer had that registration; GenOffice never created one, so .md had a ProgId with a valid command and still would not launch. Registering it makes GenOffice a first-class application for Open-with purposes.
_quoteWhy: GenOffice registered its handler unquoted: C:\Program Files\GenOffice\GenOffice.exe "%1". An unquoted path with a space is parsed as C:\Program plus arguments, so the launch fails silently - no error, no window - while 'Open with > GenOffice' still worked because that path launches the exe directly. tweaks.ps1 re-quotes these so a GenOffice update cannot reintroduce it.
_mediaWhy: These types kept a UserChoiceLatest with a hash but no ProgId, which made Windows treat them as having no default and hand them to the dead app picker. With those entries removed, the shell falls back to the HKCR default handler; re-exposing that same handler in OpenWithProgids gives a working 'Open with' submenu while the picker stays broken.
